nodes.label: Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Large-scale ecological community of plants and animals adapted to a particular climatic region. Major biomes: tropical rainforest, tropical savanna, desert, temperate grassland, temperate deciduous forest, boreal forest (taiga), tundra, and aquatic. Distribution closely related to climate zones. Each has characteristic vegetation and fauna.

nodes.label: Tropical Rainforest Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Found near the equator with high temperature (25-30C) and heavy rainfall (>2000mm) year-round. Most biodiverse biome with multi-layered canopy. Dense vegetation with tall trees, epiphytes, lianas. Poor soil despite lush growth (nutrients locked in biomass). Found in Amazon, Congo Basin, Southeast Asia. Rapid nutrient cycling.

nodes.label: Tropical Savanna Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Tropical grassland with scattered trees found between tropical forests and deserts. Distinct wet and dry seasons. Grasses dominate with fire-resistant and drought-adapted trees. Home to large herbivores and predators (African savanna: elephants, lions, zebras). Found in Africa, South America (cerrado), India, and Australia.

nodes.label: Desert Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Regions receiving less than 250mm annual rainfall with extreme temperature variations. Hot deserts (Sahara, Thar) and cold deserts (Gobi, Ladakh). Plants adapted with deep roots, small leaves, water storage (cacti, succulents). Animals are nocturnal, have water conservation adaptations. Cover about 1/5 of earth's land surface.

nodes.label: Taiga (Boreal Forest) Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Largest terrestrial biome, found between 50-70N latitude across Russia, Canada, and Scandinavia. Dominated by coniferous trees (spruce, pine, fir) adapted to cold. Long harsh winters, short cool summers. Acidic soils (podzols). Limited biodiversity. Important carbon sink. Also called boreal forest.

nodes.label: Tundra Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Treeless biome in polar regions and above treeline on mountains. Permafrost underlies the surface. Vegetation limited to mosses, lichens, grasses, and dwarf shrubs. Very short growing season (6-10 weeks). Animals include caribou, musk ox, arctic fox, snowy owl. Alpine tundra found at high altitudes in mountains globally.

nodes.label: Temperate Grassland Biome
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Grassland biome in mid-latitudes with hot summers and cold winters. Deep fertile soils (chernozem/black earth). Known by various names: prairies (North America), steppes (Eurasia), pampas (South America), veld (South Africa), downs (Australia). Heavily converted to agriculture due to rich soils. Continental climate with low rainfall.
